c.tagline: Limestone islands and warm Andaman tides.

avoid.reason: Jet-ski and motorbike rental-damage scams; drink-spiking in nightlife; high scooter-accident risk

hood_desc: The island's brashest beach resort town, famous for its long beach, packed nightlife and neon-lit Bangla Road. Ideal for party-seekers and first-timers wanting action and convenience.
A relaxed, family-friendly beach town with a broad sandy bay and a calmer vibe than nearby Patong. Best for couples and families wanting a laid-back beach holiday.
A scenic, upmarket beach area with a pretty bay, good sunsets and a moderate mix of dining and nightlife. Suits travelers wanting balance between relaxation and amenities.
The historic town center with colorful Sino-Portuguese shophouses, cafes, street art and markets. Great for culture seekers who prefer heritage charm over beaches.
A quieter, more low-key beach village popular with families and those seeking calm. Perfect for travelers wanting a peaceful, less crowded seaside stay.
lodging: Hilton Phuket Arcadia Resort and Spa
The Memory at On On Hotel

water.note: Avoid tap water; stick to bottled or purified water to prevent stomach issues.

transit.pay: There's no citywide transit card - pay drivers directly in cash (Thai baht). Shared songthaews charge a flat 30-50 THB (~$0.85-1.40) around town; the newer Phuket Smart Bus (airport-Patong-Karon-Rawai) and Grab app rides can be paid by card in-app or cash.
transit.hours: Songthaews run roughly 6am-6pm (later on Patong's main routes); there is no scheduled night transit, so tuk-tuks, taxis, or Grab cover late-night trips.
transit.note: Most visitors get around by songthaew, metered taxi, tuk-tuk, rented scooter, or the Grab ride-hailing app - there is no rail or citywide bus network.
